sample_unit: patient education topics (each generated by 2 chatbots with and without a 6th-grade prompt)

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient materials with vs without 6th-grade reading level prompt
links.effect: Prompting for a 6th-grade level significantly improved readability for both chatbots; prompted ChatGPT 4.0 reached Flesch Reading Ease 67.9 and SMOG 10.2, versus 36.5 and 14.7 unprompted.
links.quote: When prompted to produce PEM at a 6th-grade reading level, both ChatGPT 4.0 and Bard were able to significantly improve in their readability scores, with prompted ChatGPT 4.0 being able to consistently generate content that was easier to read (Flesch Reading Ease Score: 67.9, Simple Measure of Gobbledygook: 10.2).

links.outcome: Reading difficulty of unprompted AI-generated patient education materials
links.effect: Unprompted ChatGPT 4.0 material was hardest to read (FRE 36.5; SMOG 14.7); unprompted Bard was easier (FRE 52.3; SMOG 12.7), though still above a 6th-grade level.
links.quote: Across all readability indices, PEM generated by ChatGPT 4.0 consistently had the highest readability scores, indicating that the material generated by this AI chatbot may be most difficult to read in its unprompted form (Flesch Reading Ease Score: 36.5; Simple Measure of Gobbledygook: 14.7).

screen.reason: The study directly tests whether adding a 6th-grade reading level prompt constraint improves the readability metrics of AI-generated patient education materials compared to baseline unprompted generation.
